materials: PLA Turuncu / Tarçın (Elas, Porima or eSun; ~#DF6E35): crown, chin cap, body top, pods, tail rings A, hubs, ears (~95 g)
PLA Krem / Fildişi (~#F3EEE4): muzzle, belly, cheek windows, inner ears (~13 g)
PLA Antrasit / Siyah (~#2A2C31): socks, shins, tail rings B, neck, mouth, nose (~40 g); nose gloss = 2 coats of clear varnish (no PETG, no ironing on the curved nose)
+ ~18 g PLA internal frame, hub posts, neck yoke, eye bezels (in the CAD mass budget but not in the STLs)
print.basis: Net plastic from the concept STLs: shell 1.6 mm (4 perimeters) + 15 % infill -> 152 g (PLA 145 g, TPU 7 g; ears are PLA); +18 g internal frame; +10-15 % brim/support/failed-part allowance -> ~195 g filament. Every colour is a separate part, so no AMS/multi-material printer is needed, but 3 PLA colours + TPU means 4 filament set-ups. Rates: a Turkish university tariff lists 5 TL/g PLA, 6 TL/g PETG, 7 TL/g TPU (KDV incl., 200 TL minimum); pea3d.com (2026) gives hobby printers 20-40 TL/h and pro 80-150 TL/h plus material, and gram prices of 3-5x filament cost. Gram basis: 182 g PLA x 3.5-5 TL = 637-910 + 9 g TPU x 6-8 TL = 54-72 + 4 material/colour set-ups x 25-75 TL = 100-300 -> 805-1295. Hour basis: 14-22 h x 30-45 TL/h + material ~180 -> 600-1170. Studio quotes vary a lot: the concept's 450 TL floor is not realistic for 30+ small parts in 4 materials. The studio's own shipping is counted under shipping_tl.

shipping_detail.note: Free-shipping thresholds read live from each shop's header (Robotistan 1,500; Motorobit 2,500 MNG/DHL; Robolink 1,500; Direnc and Robo90 1,500). The fee below the threshold is not printed on the pages; 90-150 TL is assumed (Robot Sepeti's FAQ says 100 TL). Moving the 10 MG90S to Motorobit (151.50 each) to reach its 2,500 TL threshold would cost +257 TL to save ~120 TL, so it is not worth it.

tools_note: Only if you own none. A USB phone charger (5 V, 2 A or more) is assumed for charging: the 2S module draws up to 4 A at 5 V and charges at ~2.2 A, so a 2 A adapter just charges slower.

concept_claim.why_higher: The concept costed its small parts at 220 TL. In real shop lines they come to about 930 TL: 856 TL verified in shops plus about 75 TL to weld the 2S pack. They cover screws, wire, connectors, heat-shrink, solder, flux, glue, magnets, perfboard, headers, the power switch and the USB cable. The concept also assumed 450-900 TL for the print and 150 TL for shipping, but the order is really three parcels plus the print studio and the acrylic cutter.

lean_variant.what: Drop the spare MG90S, the VL53L0X edge sensor, the flux and the copper tape, leave the nose matte (no varnish) and take the cheaper half of the print range (a hobby studio). Formula: parts 5163.08 - 764.38 = 4398.7 + services 200-400 (acrylic visor + pack welding) + print 750-1025 + shipping 180-550 = 5528.70-6373.70, rounded. Further option, not counted: one ESP32-S3 N16R8 devkit (Direnc 610.23) in the head instead of two Super Minis saves ~335 TL but adds a Direnc parcel (~100 TL), a 12-wire neck loom and a tight fit.

changes_vs_concept: BMI160 (Direnc 127.86, still in stock) -> MPU6500 GY-6500 (Motorobit 136.35) so Direnc is not a 4th parcel; the role is the same I2C tilt/flip detection.
2S 3 A BMS -> 2S 5 A BMS (Robotistan 45.24), as the concept itself asked for >= 5 A.

14500 cells: the guide's 105.48 TL Direnc cell -> Orion 14500 900 mAh at Robotistan 94.95 (consolidates the parcel). No IMR/high-drain 14500 is sold in these shops: Direnc rates this cell 3C (~2.7 A), below the ~4.8 A battery-side recovery peak.
TTP223B and PAM8403 moved off Robo90 (to Motorobit and Robolink) to avoid a 5th parcel.
Acrylic is one mask-shaped 73 x 36 mm piece per the CAD (not 2x d32); priced as a local laser-cut job.
Added real lines for screws, nuts, wire, JST leads, headers, perfboard, caps, diodes, switch, heat-shrink, solder, flux, CA glue, copper tape, USB-C data cable, 2S pack welding.

Ears: rigid orange PLA on a pin, glued (CA). The concept's TPU ears and the magnet 'pop-off' idea are dropped, because the sim treats the ears as rigid colliders and that is what gets built. Magnets removed from the BOM.
Speaker 32 mm 1 W (the concept text and calc.json); the GLB now models it at 32 x 5 mm. To fit, the head-pan micro servo body points forward instead of back.
Nose: black PLA + clear varnish (was PETG in one file and PLA in another).
risks: Battery current: the only 14500s in stock are ~3C cells (2.7 A). Walking (~1.3 A battery side) is fine; self-righting peaks (~4.8 A for < 0.5 s) will sag the pack and may trip the 5 A BMS. A BMS trip or a brown-out mid-flip means a reset (the robot lies there until it reboots), not just a weaker kick. The MuJoCo recovery numbers assume stiff 5.5 V rails; with 0.16 N·m (a sagging pack) only 15/23 of the concept's falls recover within 4 tries and 1/23 on the first try (sim/out/sens_tau0.16.json). Mitigations: firmware staggers the hip kicks (no more than 4 servos at full torque at once), 2 x 1000 µF on the servo banks, and brown-out-safe firmware that resumes the recovery after a reset. No 2S LiPo >= 20C in stock fits the 50.5 mm bay (Tinylab 850 mAh 40C is 59 x 31 x 17 mm).
MP1584 modules are 3 A peak and about 2 A continuous; each servo bank peaks near 2.9 A during recovery.

Head-pan servo: a 76 g head on a 4 g plastic-gear micro servo (0.07 N·m). Falls back-drive it into its end stop (sim: neck_pan overshoots +-40° by a few degrees; peak gear load logged in sim/out/pan_load.json). Gear stripping is likely after repeated falls; keep 1-2 spare micro servos, or add a friction (O-ring) slip coupling at the horn. An MG90S does not fit the head next to the 32 mm speaker and eye PCBs.

Hip leads: each hip's 6 servo wires cross into the body through an arc slot and flex at the slot lip on every hip move; recovery swings the hind hips through ~145° and the front hips through ~80° in a fraction of a second, several times per recovery. Standard PVC servo leads may crack after a few thousand recoveries. Use the softest lead available (or re-lead with 28 AWG silicone wire) and treat the leads as a wear part.
GC9A01: only 18 left at Robotistan; Motorobit's round-PCB version (545.40, 112 in stock) has a different outline.
Evobond CA glue: only 2 in stock at Robolink; any 502/CA glue from a hardware store works.
Shipping fees below the free-shipping thresholds are assumed (90-150 TL), not read from the shops.
